title: Transformation dependency and data-preserving clean-cutover program
affectedPackages: Identity Directory for Organization and Person
versioning: DR-0003 and the files it governs share one revision counter, cited as DR-0003@<revision>, or DR-0003@<revision>:<artifact-id> for one gateArtifacts row (each node's consumes in S2). definition-of-done.json, non-goals.json, and journeys.json carry their own revision, raised with this record's. Adding an artifact, edge, context, or journey mapping is additive; removing a producer or moving it later, dropping or loosening a DOD item, and reordering contexts are breaking. A ratified revision pins the SHA-256 of each governed file under docs/program/, so an unapproved edit fails DR_APPROVAL_STALE.
supersession: A ratified revision is never edited. A changed decision gets a new revision that names the prior one in supersedes and gives a supersessionReason. From S2, leaf-gate fails a PR citing a breaking-superseded revision until it cites the successor (LEAF_GATE_SUPERSEDED); an additive successor passes. S3 supersedes this revision to ratify P3 and P5 against #18's ADR.
context: Issue #17 (ROUNDS-01-L03), stage S1 of four. Spec lines refer to rounds-review docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-rounds-review-board-design.md, and the catalog is rounds-review src/data/capabilities.json and src/data/capabilities.ts. The gates, gateArtifacts, and closure fields follow docs/program/program-record.schema.json. S2 adds docs/program/leaf-dag.json, its schema, scripts/conformance/rules/program.mjs, scripts/program/reconcile.mjs, and leaf-gate in report mode; S3 ratifies the context order and rollback defaults; S4 sets leaf-gate to enforce. Orchestrator decisions are taken under the owner's delegation to execute the approved plan.

securityConsequences.account: No runtime or privilege change. The program puts account isolation first (#9 to #14 in phase 1), and DOD-1 makes server-derived account scope part of every leaf's definition of done.
securityConsequences.privacy: Fixtures and examples are synthetic: the rollback fixture holds placeholder tags, commits, and digests and no account data. Transfer templates record procedures, never user data. DOD-6 keeps career content out of logs, traces, and metrics.
securityConsequences.secret: Nothing here reads or stores a secret. upgradeSource holds a release tag, commit, and image digests, which are public release metadata. S2's leaf-gate workflows get only actions: write (dispatcher) or read-only contents, issues, and pull-requests plus statuses: write, check out no PR code, and stay disabled until the owner sets LEAF_GATE_ENABLED.
securityConsequences.publicBoundary: Nothing new is published. scripts/program/report.mjs reads PR titles and issue states through the GitHub API, or from a saved state file, and writes nothing. From S2 leaf-gate posts one commit status on PRs, and only after the owner enables it.

decisions.title: Delivery follows the spec's program order
decisions.decision: Leaves are ordered by the nine phases of spec 3072-3092, not by epic letter or catalog order: (1) containment, ROUNDS-00A and ROUNDS-00B; (2) decisions and early gates: ROUNDS-01, #18's database and transaction ADR, and the early ROUNDS-34 harnesses (#170, #171, #182); (3) authority substrate: account authorization, commands and idempotency, relation integrity, the pack contract, privacy policy, and the migration journal; (4) canonical aggregates, ROUNDS-03 to ROUNDS-07; (5) ingestion substrate: ROUNDS-14 privacy, then ROUNDS-10, ROUNDS-11, and ROUNDS-12 before the full ROUNDS-09 Capture UI, with adapters in ROUNDS-13; (6) vertical slices, each shipping its commands, read model, migration, UI, tests, and retirement gate together; (7) all five practice tracks behind the Software Engineering pack; (8) ROUNDS-29 and ROUNDS-30; (9) final cutover and release proof. Milestones 0 to 7 (spec 3104-3147) group the user outcomes inside that order. A leaf moves to the phase where an earlier leaf's gate needs it: the early ROUNDS-34 harnesses sit in phase 2, and #172 to #174 in phase 3. Containment preempts: a containment fix never waits on a later phase.

alternatives.reason: ROUNDS-34 leaves in epic F gate leaves in epics A and B, so letter order deadlocks.
It puts every ROUNDS-32 transfer after all the surfaces, while spec 3083-3085 ships each slice with its own migration and retirement gate.

alternatives.option: One whole-product cutover at the end
alternatives.reason: Spec 2646-2647 rejects it; the approved direction moves one context at a time with a rollback checkpoint.

decisions.consequences: S2's leaf-dag.json gives every node a phase (1 to 9) and a milestone (0 to 7) from its refined body, and leaf-gate fails a PR whose prerequisite is still open (report mode from S2, enforce from S4).
decisions.migrationImpact: No transfer runs before containment and the substrate it uses. Transfers follow the context order in docs/program/cutover-policy.md.
decisions.rollbackImpact: Reordering is a superseding revision. One that moves a prerequisite later fails the affected PRs until they cite the successor.

decisions.title: One bounded context at a time, every migration stage owned
decisions.decision: The program moves one bounded context at a time (spec 2641-2647). A converted concept has one writable authority at every revision (DR-0002 M2), a retirement criterion, and a time-bounded compatibility window; adapters, shadow reads, and comparisons read and never write. An authorityTransfer node is the PR that ships a run plan, after its mapping leaves, with one transfer per context it lists; #163's run stages 0 to 6 are transfers inside one node. Each of the 16 migration stages (spec 2677-2695) has one owner leaf in docs/program/cutover-policy.md. #164 runs stage 16 and removes legacy paths; it switches no authority of its own.

alternatives.reason: That is the whole-product cutover spec 2646-2647 rejects.

alternatives.option: Keep legacy and canonical writers in sync
alternatives.reason: Dual writing is what the approved direction rejected (spec 2639-2647).

decisions.consequences: No two freezes overlap. A context sits in exactly one transfer node's list, and S2 fails a second. Each stage owner supplies that stage's mechanism or receipt.
decisions.migrationImpact: Data moves only through #156's framework under a transfer node's run plan, after #155's disposition manifest is complete (spec 2649-2673).
decisions.rollbackImpact: Each transfer's filled rollback template bounds its rollback. Before #164's point of no return the switch record restores the legacy writer; after it, a compensating change set (spec 772-773). A rollback replays or compensates and never discards post-switch writes (spec 2715-2716).

decisions.title: Draft context order
decisions.decision: Until S3 ratifies it against #18's ADR, the order is: M0 #14/S1 share; M1 #159 account, directory, career-profile; M2 #160/S1 to S3 pipeline, campaign, people-pursuit-notes, and #162/S1 actions; M3 #161 materials; M4 #160/S4 to S6 interview, people-round-notes, offer; M5 #163/P1 practice-0 to practice-6; then #164. docs/program/cutover-policy.md lists what S3 settles, including where the share rows' transfer sits (DR-0002@1 names #161) and #43's round types landing after the Milestone 4 interview transfer.

alternatives.reason: Opportunity-linked editions (#85) attach to the Opportunity and Pursuit that Milestone 2 migrates.
Freezes would overlap, and spec 2689 freezes one context's writes at a time.

decisions.consequences: Draft: no transfer node merges in enforce mode until S3 ratifies the order, and none can run before then anyway.
decisions.rollbackImpact: S3 supersedes this revision with the ratified order.

decisions.title: One rollback template per transferred context
decisions.decision: Every authority transfer fills docs/program/rollback-template.schema.json once per context it lists, as docs/program/transfers/<leaf>-<context>.json in its own PR (from S2). The template holds the 11 fields of spec 2703-2713 (rollback deadline, allowed downtime, recovery point and time objectives, forward and reverse compatibility, the final write-freeze boundary, the replay or reverse-delta journal, treatment of shares, exports, emails, and other external effects, partial-deploy detection, read-model downgrade or rebuild, and the decision owner), plus upgradeSource (the tag, commit, and image digests a rollback returns to) and backupConsistency. docs/program/fixtures/rollback-synthetic.json fills it with synthetic values.

alternatives.option: A database snapshot as the rollback
alternatives.reason: Spec 2699: a snapshot alone is not a valid rollback after new writes.

alternatives.option: Rollback prose in each transfer body
alternatives.reason: Nothing checks prose, so a transfer could ship without a deadline or a journal.

decisions.consequences: From S2 a transfer PR without a valid template for a listed context fails LEAF_GATE_NO_ROLLBACK. The operator passes the file to #156's switch as the transfer record.
decisions.migrationImpact: Each transfer's rollback is bounded before its freeze starts.
decisions.rollbackImpact: A template revision that only adds optional fields is additive; a new required field is breaking for open transfer PRs.

decisions.title: Rollback defaults
decisions.decision: Until S3 ratifies them against #18's benchmark: the final write freeze lasts at most 15 minutes, zero accepted writes are lost, rollback or restore takes at most 30 minutes at the scale floor, and restore is rehearsed rather than inferred from a successful backup. A transfer may tighten a default; loosening one needs a deviations entry with the owner's approval.

alternatives.reason: Spec 2062-2067 sets program-wide targets, and #156, #159, and #161 already size their freezes to them.

decisions.consequences: The template's deviations list makes every loosened default visible in review.
decisions.migrationImpact: Freezes and batch sizes are planned inside the defaults.
decisions.rollbackImpact: S3 supersedes this revision; a tighter ratified default is breaking for templates that relied on the draft value.

decisions.title: Gate artifacts, one producer each
decisions.decision: Each of the 20 gate strings splits into artifacts, one gateArtifacts row each, and each row has exactly one producer: a leaf or stage, or, for an artifact every authority-matrix row needs, the DR-0002 field naming that row's producer (command_owner.leaf for U0's ERD rows and U1's aggregate and state-machine contracts, transfer.mapping for U10's mappings), so nothing here copies an owner DR-0002 records. A producer isn't blocked by the artifact it creates (spec 3232-3236); its body states the exemption, and its acceptance criteria deliver the artifact and its evidence. Consumers bind by domain. requiredFor forces U4 on #43 and #130 to #137, U8 on #133 to #135, and U9 on #93, #94, and #161, whatever their archetype. Rows whose producer has landed on next say where the artifact lives.

alternatives.reason: No body names U8 and #43 lacks U4, so code-running practice and the pack migration would ship without their gates.
C7 alone has four producers, so a gate couldn't be met in part, and a missing producer would hide behind the others.

alternatives.option: Copy each matrix row's owner into this table
alternatives.reason: Two records of one owner drift, and DR-0002's rule already fails a row without exactly one command owner.

decisions.consequences: S2's program.mjs fails an artifact without exactly one producer and a requiredFor nobody consumes. scripts/program/report.mjs computes ROUNDS-01 closure from these rows, and scripts/program/lib.mjs checks that every row resolves, in the conformance tests until program.mjs takes it over.
decisions.rollbackImpact: A changed producer is a superseding revision. Removing a producer or moving it later is breaking and returns its consumers to blocked.

decisions.title: ROUNDS-01 closes last and gates no leaf
decisions.decision: ROUNDS-01 closes once #15, #16, this leaf's S4, and every producer of a U0 to U11 artifact have merged. DR-0001 correction 1 moved U0, U1, U2, and U11 out of the filed gate of #15 to #17 and into this closure. Closure gates no leaf: a leaf waits only on the artifacts it consumes. scripts/program/report.mjs prints it.

alternatives.option: Keep U0, U1, U2, and U11 as this leaf's filed gate
alternatives.reason: #18 to #26 and #39 to #43 depend on this leaf and produce those artifacts, a cycle.

alternatives.option: Close on the first three gate items
alternatives.reason: Spec 3195 puts the whole universal gate before completing ROUNDS-01.

decisions.consequences: ROUNDS-01 stays open until late in the program, which blocks nothing.
decisions.rollbackImpact: A superseding revision can change the condition; closure never reopens a leaf.

decisions.title: Definition of done and the non-goals register
decisions.decision: docs/program/definition-of-done.json (revision 1) holds DOD-1 to DOD-7: account-authorized, expected version, idempotent, revisioned and audited, one writable authority, correlation and redaction, and DESIGN.md plus a design review for surface leaves. From S2 each node's dod names the items it meets. docs/program/non-goals.json holds the product non-goals (spec 177-184 with their PRODUCT.md counterparts), every catalog tradeoffs entry verbatim, and the reference leaf issue.

alternatives.option: Each body writes its own definition of done
alternatives.reason: 176 bodies would drift, and no check could tell which leaf skipped idempotency.

decisions.consequences: Dropping or loosening a DOD item needs the owner's approval in a superseding revision; adding or tightening one is additive.
decisions.rollbackImpact: Supersede; a dropped item is breaking for the nodes that cite it.

decisions.title: Reference leaf issue
decisions.decision: Default taken under the owner's delegation: #18 (ROUNDS-02-L01), the refinement's suggestion, is gate U11's one fully populated reference leaf issue. The owner designates another by superseding this revision.

alternatives.option: No reference issue until the owner picks
alternatives.reason: 45 bodies name gate U11, and nothing produced its reference issue.

decisions.consequences: The U11.reference-leaf row names #18 with designation default.
decisions.rollbackImpact: A superseding revision names another leaf; additive for every consumer.

decisions.title: Primary journeys mapped to leaves
decisions.decision: docs/program/journeys.json maps each step of the five primary journeys to one leaf, the milestone where the step first works, and the readiness gate it waits on, and names each journey's completing leaf for #173. First run is the Today empty state of #145, then the Career Profile empty state of #26, then openCapture from #49 listing the sources of #65, with no second chooser. Profile completeness explanations (spec 1030), which #65 leaves to this leaf, go to #26.

alternatives.reason: #173 registers the journeys and needs an owner for each; spec 1030 had none.

alternatives.option: A source chooser on the Career Profile empty state
alternatives.reason: A second chooser for the same sources, which the one Capture Center replaces.

decisions.consequences: Giving spec 1030 to #26 is a body change the owner re-authorizes with item 4 of docs/program/reauthorization.md.
decisions.rollbackImpact: A superseding revision remaps a step; additive unless it moves a step to a later milestone.

decisions.title: One owner re-authorization before the DAG
decisions.decision: docs/program/reauthorization.md orders the rounds-review changes for one owner authorization, items 1 to 8, starting with per-leaf state in the filer so issues:file never reopens a completed leaf. Its edge table records the edges S2's DAG adds or drops, among them #13, #19, #29, #37, and #47 on #10 (ROUNDS-00B-L02). Until the re-authorization receipt, leaf-gate enforces the filed prerequisites (edgeSet filed), and then the proposed ones. Only the owner regenerates leaf-dag.json, from the catalog.

alternatives.reason: issues:file reverts any body the catalog doesn't carry.

alternatives.option: Apply the changes one body at a time
alternatives.reason: Each run re-renders every body, and until item 1 every run reopens closed leaves.

decisions.consequences: S2 is built after item 6. Until the receipt, scripts/program/report.mjs lists the table's edges as pending.
decisions.rollbackImpact: An unapplied item can be dropped in a superseding revision; an applied one is undone by a later catalog change and export.

decisions.title: leaf-gate ships disabled, then reports, then enforces
decisions.decision: S2's leaf-gate-dispatch.yml and leaf-gate.yml ship disabled: every job runs only when vars.LEAF_GATE_ENABLED == 'true', so no dispatch fires and no status posts until the owner sets that variable, together with the main ruleset that requires the leaf-gate status. From then leaf-gate runs in report mode (success, with the code it would fail in the description) until S4 sets docs/program/leaf-gate.json to enforce. No agent runs workflow_dispatch; only the owner-enabled dispatcher does.

alternatives.reason: The dispatcher would call workflow_dispatch on main for agent PRs, which the execution rules forbid, and nothing requires the status before the owner's ruleset.

alternatives.option: Check out PR code in pull_request_target
alternatives.reason: That runs untrusted code with a write token; leaf-gate.yml reads only base-tip files and the PR's transfer templates as data.

decisions.consequences: Until the owner enables it, the conformance job and scripts/program/report.mjs are the program's signal.
decisions.rollbackImpact: The owner unsets LEAF_GATE_ENABLED, or an owner PR with program:override sets leaf-gate.json back to report.

decisions.title: Edge kinds, stage nodes, and work in progress
decisions.decision: A leaf is merged once its [LEAF-ID] PR or every stage PR merges, and done once a merged PR closed its issue as completed. Stage IDs are the body's per-PR labels (S<n>, S<letter>, P<n>, and #2's step numbers); a multi-PR stage gets one .k node per PR (ROUNDS-32-L10/SB.3). An edge's kind is done (the prerequisite is done), merged (merged, open or not), or closure (it gates only the dependent's closing PR). Open, non-draft PRs cover at most one authorityTransfer node, two implementation leaves, and one architecture-decision leaf; the next fails LEAF_GATE_WIP. Containment preempts and doesn't count.

alternatives.reason: #30 and #168/S2 deadlock: each waits for the other's closing PR.
Parallel transfer PRs would race for the one-context-at-a-time rollout.

decisions.consequences: scripts/program/report.mjs parses titles this way today; S2's leaf-gate applies the kinds and the limit.
decisions.migrationImpact: Transfers run after merge, under #156's one-context-at-a-time rollout; the limit covers only open PRs.
decisions.rollbackImpact: A superseding revision changes a kind or the limit.

gateArtifacts.note: Default taken (decision P9); the owner designates another by superseding this record.

closure.rule: ROUNDS-01 closes once these have merged and every producer of an artifact for these gates has merged; closure gates no leaf (decision P7).

departures.title: Stage owners work with other leaves
departures.detail: Each migration stage names one owner leaf, as the issue asks, plus the leaves it works with. Stages 6 to 14 are #156's mechanisms, run by each transfer node for each context it lists.

departures.title: Per-row producers
departures.detail: U0's ERD rows, U1's aggregate contracts, and U10's mappings name their producer through DR-0002's command_owner.leaf and transfer.mapping fields instead of one gateArtifacts row per matrix row.

departures.title: Edges beyond item 2
departures.detail: The edge table in docs/program/reauthorization.md also carries the edges #1, #16, #151, and #155 ask this leaf to record, and the orchestrator's five edges on #10.

departures.title: Numbered stage labels
departures.detail: #2's PRs are labeled by step number ([ROUNDS-00A-L02/1]), so the stage grammar accepts a number as well as S<n>, S<letter>, and P<n>.

departures.title: Checks before program.mjs
departures.detail: S1 ships scripts/program/lib.mjs, whose checks the conformance tests run against these files; S2's program.mjs runs them in the conformance job.

departures.title: Verbatim quote of the ROUNDS-32 tradeoff
departures.detail: The issue wants every catalog tradeoff verbatim, and DR-0001 G11 fails a new unqualified use of the cutover phrase, which the ROUNDS-32 tradeoff contains. non-goals.json keeps the quote verbatim with one space written as a JSON \u0020 escape, so the parsed text matches the catalog and G11's raw-text check doesn't count the quotation. Allowlisting the line instead would take a DR-0001 revision.
